svg.title: A client reports painless bright red bleeding with bowel movements and rectal itching, but denies pain with sitting and has no tender external lumps. Which problem does the nurse suspect, and what teaching is indicated?
svg.desc: INTERNAL EQUALS INVISIBLE - PAINLESS BLEEDING AND ITCHING, while EXTERNAL EQUALS EXPOSED - pain with sitting, pain with bowel movements and tender lumps, which this client does not have. Hemorrhoids are swollen VEINS from too much pressure - a vascular problem, not a skin problem - so treatment targets the straining: high fiber and fluids, warm sitz baths, a donut cushion and analgesic ointments. A pilonidal cyst is an infected hair follicle at the top of the gluteal cleft, and a strangulated hernia involves trapped bowel with no blood supply.
